_comment: Google Business Profile discovery for the SEO-target properties, run 2026-09-21 via the Places Text Search API (the sanctioned path; scraping Google results is ruled out). Searched each property three ways: business name + city + state, exact phone number, and exact domain. Field mask restricted to id, name, address, phone, website and business status -- no ratings, reviews or photos, per the Places terms constraint that governs the mattress directory and applies equally here.
_absence_caveat: A property listed as not_found is NOT proven to have no GBP. Unverified and suspended profiles do not appear in the Places API at all, so this method can confirm a profile exists but cannot confirm one does not. The definitive check is signing in to business.google.com on the owning Google account, which only Mitch can do.

lake-charles-fences.gbp_address: 908 Audubon St, Lake Charles, LA 70601, USA
nap_notes: Name differs in one word: site says 'Lake Charles Fences & Decks', GBP says '...and Decks'. Citations key on exact-string consistency, so pick one and use it everywhere.
The GBP publishes a street address the website does not carry at all. Adding it to site.json would strengthen the LocalBusiness schema and give citations a real NAP to match.

scaffolding-los-angeles.gbp_address: 3515 S Norton Ave, Los Angeles, CA 90018, USA
nap_notes: URGENT: the profile is flagged CLOSED_PERMANENTLY. A closed GBP is suppressed in Maps and local packs, so this property currently cannot rank locally no matter what the website does.
Phone matches the site exactly (323-498-3395), so the profile is definitely ours rather than a similarly named business.
Reopening is done from the GBP dashboard and needs the owning Google account.
The GBP publishes a street address the website does not carry.

not_found._note: No profile surfaced for the business name, the published phone, or the domain. See _absence_caveat before concluding these do not exist.

not_searchable.seacoast-hurricane-shutters: Contact details were removed from the site on 2026-09-21 while its positioning is decided, so there is no phone to search on.

implication: The brief's premise -- that aged Google Business Profiles already exist across the portfolio -- is confirmed for two properties and unconfirmed for eleven, including Twin City Fences, which was nominated as the pilot. Citation building depends on a real, verifiable NAP; without a GBP there is nothing to make citations consistent WITH, and creating listings for a business that is not eligible is the failure mode that costs an entire Google account. This needs resolving before the citation phase starts.
